title: Premium, discount & OTE
subtitle: Buying cheap and selling expensive, ICT style

scenes.say: Buy cheap, sell expensive. ICT measures cheap and expensive with one simple tool: the dealing range. Here's how it works.

scenes.title: The dealing range
scenes.say: Start with an impulse swing: a fast move from a swing low to a swing high. Those two points form your dealing range. Everything inside it is either cheap or expensive.

scenes.title: Equilibrium splits the range
scenes.say: Cut the range in half. The fifty percent line is equilibrium, or fair value. Above it is premium, where smart money likes to sell. Below it is discount, where smart money likes to buy.

scenes.title: Optimal trade entry (OTE)
scenes.say: In a bullish market, don't chase the high. Wait for a pullback into discount, ideally the optimal trade entry zone, between sixty-two and seventy-nine percent of the swing. The sweet spot is seventy point five. Then target the old high and the buy stops above it.

scenes.title: The mirror for shorts
scenes.say: For shorts, flip it. Measure from the swing high down to the swing low, wait for price to retrace up into premium and the OTE zone, then sell, targeting the sell stops below the old lows.

items.label: Bearish swing
items.sub: Measure from the high down to the low

scenes.title: Rules of thumb
scenes.say: A few rules of thumb. In strong trends, discount prices don't stay long, so expect fast moves away. If price breaks below the OTE and takes an old low, look for a turtle soup long rather than panic. And always measure the most recent impulse swing.
points: Breaks the OTE and takes an old low? Look for a turtle soup long
Always measure the latest impulse swing

els.sub: The line between cheap and expensive

scenes.title: Recap
scenes.say: So: find the dealing range, buy in discount and sell in premium, and let the OTE zone give you a precise, low-risk entry.

els.sub: Wait for the 62–79% OTE zone inside the dealing range.
